# Short breaks and error rates in manual data entry

## Abstract

We measured how short breaks affect the error rate of manual data entry. In a study of 48 clerks, a five-minute break every hour lowered the error rate from 2.4% to 1.6%. The effect was largest in the afternoon.

## Introduction

Data entry errors are costly to find and correct (Ito, 2015). Earlier work linked them to fatigue (Mori and Abe, 2018), but did not test breaks of a fixed length.

## Method

We recruited 48 clerks from three offices. The setup is shown in Figure 1. Each clerk entered order forms for four weeks, with and without a five-minute break every hour, following the design of Kato (2020).

## Results

Without breaks, the error rate was 2.4%; with breaks, it was 1.6% (Figure 2). Table 1 gives the rate by time of day.

The errors fell into four types: wrong digits 45%, missing fields 30%, swapped fields 20% and other 5%.

## Discussion

The effect was largest in the afternoon, which agrees with the fatigue account (Mori and Abe, 2018). A longer study is needed to see whether the effect lasts.
